summary: Shiv Singh is an Indian history, archaeology, and Indology scholar. He earned his PhD at Gurukula Kangri Vishwavidyalaya (2018–2024) and held a postdoctoral researcher position at the Indian Council of Social Science Research in 2026.

Shivram Dattatray Joshi was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Daniel H. H. Ingalls at Harvard (~1960–1964). He served at Savitribai Phule Pune University (~1964–2002; professor ~1974–1986) and led Deccan College's Sanskrit Dictionary Department (~1987–1996).

Shizuka Sasaki is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Kyoto University, UC Berkeley, and Bukkyo University, and under Jikido Takasaki. He has held positions at Hanazono University, becoming Professor of Indian Buddhism in 2002.

Shlomo Pines (1908–1990) worked in philosophy, Indology, and religious studies. He studied at Heidelberg, Geneva, and Humboldt University of Berlin (1926–1934), and later taught at the University of Paris, IHST, and the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (1952–1990).

Shmuel Sambursky (1900–1990) was a scholar of philosophy and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Königsberg (~1919–1923) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1923–1924), and held a long-term post at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1928–1970).

Shobha Rani Dash is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. Her academic appointments include a research post at Ryukoku University in 2010, lecturer at Otani University (attested 2012), and professor at the Otani Academic Society (attested 2026).
Shodo Fujita is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University under Shoko Takeuchi. He served as a visiting researcher at Ryukoku University (attested 1995–2013).
Shodo Harada is a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Shofuku-ji under Mumon Yamada (~1962–1982). He served as abbot at Sōgen-ji starting in 1982 and founded Tahoma Sogenji Zen Monastery in 1995.

Shodo Yamagami is an Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed doctoral coursework at Kyoto University (~1962–1964) and had a long academic career at Kyoto Sangyo University, serving as assistant professor (~1974–1988) and professor (~1988–2009).

Shogo Watanabe is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Toyo University. He taught at Toyo University (~1989–1996; professor ~2003–2024), Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (~2024), and Taisho University (attested 2026).

Shohaku Okumura is a Buddhist studies scholar and teacher. He studied at Komazawa University and under Kosho Uchiyama. He served at Pioneer Valley Zendo, Minnesota Zen Meditation Center, and directed the Soto Zen Buddhism International Center (1997–2010).
Shoichi Ozawa (1929–2012) was a scholar in Japanology and history/archaeology. He studied at Waseda University (~1948–1952) and held an academic post at The Open University of Japan (~1990–2000).

Shoji Mori is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Toyo University and under Giyu Nishi. He taught at Toyo University as assistant professor (~1977–1984) and professor (~1984–2009), and was a researcher at Okurayama Institute.

Shoji Muramoto is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. He studied at Kyoto University and the University of Zurich, and held posts at Hanazono University and Kobe City University of Foreign Studies (attested 2002–2009).
Shoju Inaba (1915–1990) specialized in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as a professor at Otani University (~1958–1986) and as a part-time lecturer at Nagoya University.

Shojun Bando (1932–2004) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1951–1956). He held academic posts at Ueno Gakuen University (~1961–1977) and Otani University (~1977–1998).

Shokin Furuta was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and Tokyo University of Education under Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki. He served as professor at Hokkaido (~1956–1968) and Nihon University (~1968–1982).
Shoko Kanaoka (1930–2004) was a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies who served as a professor at Toyo University (attested 1987, 2000).

Shoko Miyabayashi (1932–2014) was a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar. He studied at Taisho University (1948–1955), where he also spent his academic career as lecturer (1960), assistant professor (1962), and Dean of Buddhist Studies (1978–2002).

Shoko Miyata is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology, attested in 2026 as a lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.
